source: STEER Project (Save the Children, iDE Cambodia, and the Cambodian Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries) - "Guide on Banana Cultivation Techniques" (សៀវភៅណែនាំស្តីអំពី បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះដំណាំចេក), February 2020
text:
Chek Namva (ចេកណាំវ៉ា) is one of Cambodia's most widely grown banana varieties, sometimes described as growing well almost everywhere. Its bunches carry medium-sized fruit with a moderately thick skin and are recognized for tolerating a range of growing conditions without needing highly specialized care.

Because it is so widely adapted, Namva was used as one of three Cambodian "local check" varieties (alongside Chek Pong Moan and Chek Ambong) in the Prek Leap National School of Agriculture's national banana variety trial - a sign of its status as a benchmark variety that imported types are compared against.
